### Ramp Type Digital Voltmeter (DVM)
The ramp-type DVM converts an unknown analog DC voltage into a time interval using a linear ramp generator, and then measures this time interval using electronic digital counters.

### Working Principle
1. **Start of Measurement Cycle:** A negative-going or positive-going linear ramp voltage is initiated by a ramp generator. Simultaneously, a main gate circuit opens, allowing clock pulses from a stable oscillator to pass into a decimal counter.
2. **Voltage Comparison:** The linear ramp voltage is continuously compared with the unknown input DC voltage ($V_{in}$) using an electronic voltage comparator.
3. **Stop of Measurement Cycle:** When the ramp voltage equals $V_{in}$, the comparator generates a pulse that closes the main gate. 
4. **Display:** The number of clock pulses counted during this time interval is directly proportional to the magnitude of the input voltage and is displayed visually on digital readout tubes.

```
[Input Voltage] ---> [Comparator] <--- [Ramp Generator]
                           |
                     [Main Gate]
                           ^
[Clock Oscillator] --------|
                           |
                     [Decade Counter] ---> [Digital Display]
```
proTip: Emphasize that the core conversion technique in this DVM is Voltage-to-Time conversion followed by Time-to-Digital count.
